subject: Deployment mode qualification: hosted vs dedicated - follow-up
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode qualification: hosted vs dedicated - notes & next steps

Hi Samantha -

Thanks again for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so we can size the right deployment mode for Acme Analytics.

Call highlights:
- Primary workload: real-time analytics enrichment for customer-facing dashboards.
- Peak traffic: likely spiky (ETL windows + bursty API calls), need to understand peak QPS and 95th/99th latency targets.
- Data sensitivity: some datasets are regulated; you mentioned a mix of lower-sensitivity and a few critical pipelines that require strict isolation.

Redwood deployment options we covered:
- Hosted API (shared): fastest to get started, cost-effective, automatic scaling. Good if strict tenant-level isolation is not required.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and stronger isolation boundaries (noisy-neighbor mitigations, capacity reservations).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full network isolation and customer-managed control plane for regulated workloads.

Open items we need from your side to recommend a path:
1) Expected peak QPS and average request size (tokens). Example: peak concurrent requests, average tokens in/out.
2) Latency SLOs (95th and 99th targets) and whether strict SLO guarantees are required for the critical pipelines.
3) Isolation requirement: is multi-tenant shared infrastructure acceptable for all workloads, or do certain pipelines need guaranteed hardware isolation?
4) Compliance needs (SOC 2 / HIPAA / contract language) and timeline for procurement.

Attachments: I attached a short one-pager on Dedicated capacity and a SOC 2 evidence checklist so your security team can preview what we can provide.

Next steps: if you're available, let's schedule a technical deep-dive next week with your infra lead (Tom) and our infra/product engineering. We'll bring a sizing estimate (GPU count) and a Mutual Action Plan draft. Suggested slots: Wed 5/13 10-11am PT or Thu 5/14 2-3pm PT.

Thanks - I’ll follow up with calendar invites once you confirm a time.

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-capacity-one-pager.pdf, SOC2-evidence-list.xlsx

Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification: hosted vs dedicated - notes & next steps

Hi Priyom -

Thanks for the clear recap. A few answers from our side to help you size things:
- Expected peak: ~1200 QPS during our busiest hourly windows; average request size ~450 tokens in + 300 tokens out.
- Latency targets: 95th <= 300ms, 99th ideally < 600ms. The customer dashboards are sensitive to tail latency.
- Isolation: for our data enrichment pipelines that touch PII we need strong isolation - we cannot have compute-level noisy neighbor interference for those requests. For some non-sensitive models, multi-tenant shared infra is acceptable.
- Compliance: SOC 2 required; procurement timeline aims to close PO in ~6-8 weeks.

Questions from Tom (cc'd):
- What specific noisy-neighbor mitigations does Redwood offer on Dedicated? Any SLO guarantees or credits tied to noisy-neighbor incidents?
- Can you provide an expected lead time for Dedicated pool provisioning and a rough cost delta vs Hosted?

We can do the technical deep-dive. Tom - are you available Wed 5/13 10-11am PT?

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of Platform, Acme Analytics
Samantha.Lee@acme.com

Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification: hosted vs dedicated - notes & next steps

Thanks Samantha & Tom - great data, this is super helpful.

Quick answers inline to Tom's questions, we'll cover details in the deep-dive:
- Noisy-neighbor mitigations (high level): dedicated GPU pools with per-tenant resource reservations, strict scheduling policies, GPU cgroup/NUMA isolation where possible, and per-tenant queuing so a single noisy workload won't queue all requests. We also support model pinning to ensure critical pipelines use reserved model instances.
- SLOs & credits: for Dedicated we can include latency SLOs at contract time with service credits for breaches. Hosted has best-effort SLAs but not the same contractual latency guarantees.
- Lead time & cost: Dedicated pools typically provision in 2-4 weeks depending on GPU type and region; cost delta varies by commitment size - we'll provide a preliminary ballpark in the deep-dive.

Next steps:
- Confirm deep-dive: Wed 5/13 10-11am PT works for our infra engineers (I’ll send a calendar invite).
- We'll prepare a Mutual Action Plan and a capacity estimate for both Dedicated and Hosted hybrid approaches (so you can compare).

Forwarding Tom & Samantha's replies to our infra/product team to prepare the sizing and an initial set of SLO options.

Best,
Priyom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification: hosted vs dedicated - internal notes

Internal - quick recommendations before the deep-dive:

1) For Acme's mix of sensitivity and high QPS I recommend proposing Dedicated capacity with isolated GPU pools for the PII pipelines and a hybrid approach (Hosted for non-sensitive workloads). This keeps cost-effectiveness while giving contractual isolation where needed.

2) Noisy-neighbor mitigations to present:
- Physical/soft isolation: dedicated GPU pools with tenant affinity and node pinning for critical workloads.
- Resource reservations: guaranteed vGPU reservations or slot-based allocation to prevent single-tenant saturation.
- Scheduling & cgroups: enforce CPU/GPU cgroups and NUMA awareness to reduce cross-tenant interference.
- Per-tenant request queues + rate limiting: prevents head-of-line blocking from a bursty tenant.
- Model pinning & fallback: allow critical pipelines to pin to warmed model instances; fallback rules to lower-cost variants on failure.

3) SLOs: prepare a few SLO tiers (e.g., 95th 200ms, 95th 300ms) with corresponding contractual credits and estimated GPU reservations. Be ready to show historical percentiles from similar customers.

Action items:
- Priyom: capture Acme's exact token sizes and peak concurrency in the MAP.
- Ben: can you run a quick sizing calc for 1200 QPS at ~750 tokens/request (combined) and draft cost delta options?
- I’ll prepare slide notes on noisy-neighbor mitigations and a starter SLO schedule for the contract.

-Marissa
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
